ORG-03: Check effective key creation and upload restrictions, default service account grant constraints and exception projects. Reconcile guardrails with existing keys. ORG-04: Map actual resource locations, backups and service-supported location constraints to contractual requirements. Identify global services and processing paths that need separate analysis. STO-05: Reconcile Data Access settings, bucket access patterns, storage-transfer resources and owner-provided transfer histories. Inspect service-agent permissions and external destinations. DAT-01: Inspect public and private addresses, authorized networks, TLS requirements, flags and IAM database authentication. Request database-native user and grant evidence; project IAM is only part of the review. DAT-02: Inspect availability type, backups, point-in-time recovery and replica configuration for the actual database engine. Review past restore records and dependent encryption keys. DAT-03: Use dataset and table asset metadata plus approved exports of row policies, policy tags, masking rules and authorized views. Trace inherited IAM, dataset ACLs and data-sharing links. DAT-04: Inspect dataset locations, encryption, expirations, reservations and job-history evidence supplied by owners. Review copies, extracts and scheduled transfers without running SQL jobs. DAT-05: Identify Spanner, Firestore, Bigtable, AlloyDB, Redis and data-processing services from inventory. Apply service-specific access, network, encryption, availability and backup tests using owner-provided metadata where native collectors are absent. KEY-01: Inspect secret metadata, replication, IAM, labels and owners. Trace read and administration privileges while never accessing secret payloads. KEY-02: List version metadata, status and dates; inspect rotation notifications, automation records and deployment version references. A rotation schedule is not proof the secret changed. KEY-03: Inspect key rings, algorithms, protection level, IAM and encrypt/decrypt versus administration permissions. Map key projects and service agents to protected resources. KEY-04: Review primary versions, rotation and destruction schedule evidence. Reconcile disabled or pending-destruction versions with active data and backup dependencies. KEY-05: Map required CMEK coverage and EKM or HSM requirements to actual resource metadata and service support. Review provider outages, key access and previous recovery evidence. LOG-01: Read organization, ancestor-folder and project auditConfigs, service exceptions and exempted principals. Map enabled services to the required ADMIN_READ, DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE coverage. LOG-02: Inspect project and organization sinks, inclusion and exclusion filters, destination ownership and writer grants. Review intercepting behavior and aggregated child scope. LOG-03: Inspect log bucket retention, location, access restrictions and lock state across all used locations. Reconcile SIEM and archive retention outside Cloud Logging. LOG-04: Select a known historical approved administrative or data event from a ticket. Trace it through source logging, sink routing, destination and detection within a bounded UTC window. LOG-05: Review log administration, private-log viewing, deletion and sink modification privileges. Reconcile coverage counts and missing-access errors before concluding about activity. SEC-01: Reconcile activation scope, edition, data location, services, detectors and project population with expected coverage. Read findings and record activation or permission failures. SEC-02: Sample active findings, muted records and ticket links. Evaluate severity, exploitability, asset criticality, owner, age and suppression justification. SEC-03: Map priority threats to required logs, analytics, alert routes and past incident or exercise records. Inspect existing test results rather than injecting attacks. SEC-04: Review contacts, evidence preservation, organization access, service-account revocation and network isolation procedures. Compare responsibilities against a previous incident or tabletop. SEC-05: Trace a sample of historical incidents through scope, root-cause evidence, notification decisions and verified corrective actions. Compare recurring SCC findings and logs. BCP-01: Join critical services to data stores, identities, keys, DNS, networking and provider dependencies. Obtain business-approved RPO and RTO, including data-loss tolerance. BCP-02: Reconcile data-bearing resources with snapshot, SQL backup, GKE backup and Backup and DR metadata. Inspect retention, separation, vault protection and administration. BCP-03: Read existing backup metadata and hash supplied prior restore reports. Review restored scope, timestamp, data integrity checks, elapsed time and business acceptance. BCP-04: Inspect multi-zone or regional configurations and compare capacity, quotas and dependencies to the failover design. Evaluate existing exercises and their assumptions. BCP-05: Review recovery runbooks, access prerequisites, communications and retrospective improvements. Verify named owners can locate retained evidence and necessary approvals. DEV-01: Inspect Cloud Build triggers, event filters, approval settings, repository connections and execution identities. Reconcile branch protection and contributor permissions from the source platform. DEV-02: Review build service accounts, worker pools, network access and secret references. Inspect a bounded sample of historical builds without triggering builds. DEV-03: Inspect repository locations, format, IAM and cleanup policies; obtain scan status, SBOM and exception evidence for deployed digests. DEV-04: Inspect delivery pipelines, Binary Authorization policy and approved attestor evidence. Trace one deployed artifact to source, build, approval and admission result. DEV-05: Compare current resource exports with approved infrastructure-as-code state and change records. Trace risky IAM, firewall and policy changes in the audit sample. AI-01: Inventory Vertex AI endpoints, models and datasets across approved regions; reconcile managed generative services, agent runtimes and external model integrations from application records. AI-02: Review model-specific data governance, prompt logging, grounding, caches, tuning data and retention settings against the actual contract and feature. Do not equate training restrictions with zero retention. AI-03: Inspect endpoint networking, IAM, service identities, keys and data-store permissions. Reconcile who can deploy, invoke, tune or change the runtime. AI-04: Use application-supplied agent manifests, tool definitions, retrieval ACL design and existing evaluation traces. Review delegated identity and approval of consequential actions without invoking tools. AI-05: Inspect model/version approvals, evaluation criteria, safety filters, monitoring, rollback and incident records. Sample completed evaluations for representative failure modes. OPS-01: Join workload inventory to approved SLIs, SLOs, dashboards, alerts and escalation owners from monitoring exports. Review existing incidents and error budgets. OPS-02: Inspect project quotas and obtain service-specific regional quota and utilization exports. Compare peak, growth and failover requirements to available headroom. OPS-03: Reconcile service versions, runtimes, release channels and dependencies to supported lifecycles. Review maintenance exclusions, support plans and upgrade ownership. OPS-04: Trace sampled production changes to approvals, tests, deployment records and post-change verification. Include emergency changes and supplier access. OPS-05: Reconcile ownership labels and on-call records with real responders, dependency owners and postmortem actions. FIN-01: Read billing associations for approved projects and compare with finance-approved account and cost-center records. Billing account scope requires explicit independent approval. FIN-02: Inspect budgets for explicitly approved accounts, filters, thresholds and recipients. Determine whether a budget is alerts-only or a supported spend-cap configuration and inspect actual handling. FIN-03: Reconcile labels and tags to approved allocation rules and existing billing-export configuration. Request owner-supplied query results; do not submit BigQuery jobs from the collector. FIN-04: Compare idle resource and utilization evidence with existing recommendations, commitments and business demand. Validate savings assumptions and contractual terms with finance. FIN-05: Correlate spending anomalies, identity activity and public exposure with approved workloads. Review response authority and previous cost incidents. COM-01: Identify applicable contracts, jurisdictional requirements and adopted frameworks with the organization. Map obligations to services, data, controls and evidence owners rather than assuming provider certification transfers. COM-02: Compare data classification and existing discovery/profile results with storage, databases, datasets and AI inventories. Inspect coverage, location, job recency and exclusions without initiating scans. COM-03: Trace selected data flows through collection, purpose, sharing, retention, deletion and backups using owner-provided records. Resolve legal hold and recovery obligations with the accountable team. COM-04: Identify Assured Workloads, access approvals, transparency logs, regional restrictions and contractual support commitments where applicable. Inspect actual control package and exceptions. COM-05: Check findings against criteria, affected population, reproducible evidence and contrary explanations. Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure.
P05.criterion: GOV-01: Every expected project has a disposition, owner and applicable control set; unexplained inventory gaps remain open. GOV-02: The responsibility matrix covers all material services and has accountable owners. GOV-03: Separation and centralized controls meet the documented design or have risk-accepted exceptions. GOV-04: Each material exception has a current owner, time limit and tested compensating control. GOV-05: Creation and retirement records reconcile to inventory without orphaned ownership, data or access. IAM-01: Each effective privileged access path is justified, assigned to an accountable identity and periodically reviewed. IAM-02: Approved authentication requirements cover human privileged paths and exceptions have independent evidence. IAM-03: Access changes meet the company's approved service levels and retain evidence of review. IAM-04: Emergency access remains usable under the stated failure scenario and accountable; temporary privilege expires as designed. IAM-05: Access analysis includes applicable allow, deny and boundary effects; unsupported permission coverage is acknowledged. WID-01: Privileged machine identities have specific purposes and accountable owners; default identities receive no unexplained broad access. WID-02: Every user-managed key is justified and managed within the company's approved lifecycle, with a keyless migration decision. WID-03: Trust restricts intended external tenants and subjects; broad pools and impersonation grants are justified. WID-04: Privilege reviews cover combined deployment and identity capabilities, including cross-project service accounts. WID-05: Activity review can distinguish expected automation from unexplained identity use without treating absence of logs as inactivity. ORG-01: Expected constraints are effective at the intended descendants; list output alone is insufficient. ORG-02: The chosen sharing policy and actual external principals match approved collaboration needs. ORG-03: The intended prevention policies and legacy-key cleanup are both evidenced. ORG-04: Approved location requirements apply to the relevant resource types and operational copies; unsupported services are documented. ORG-05: Guardrails relied upon by the audit are enforced for the intended operations, with reviewed changes and exceptions. NET-01: Public and lateral paths are justified after effective rule evaluation; a single broad rule is a review candidate, not automatic proof of reachability. NET-02: Each critical public service has the agreed protections on its actual serving path. NET-03: Private access and egress controls match the approved traffic model and observable flows. NET-04: The perimeter protects the intended supported services and approved cross-boundary paths in enforced configuration. NET-05: Telemetry supports the agreed detection use cases; name resolution and DNS change ownership are controlled. HYB-01: Host and service project responsibilities and permissions preserve the approved separation. HYB-02: Redundancy and routing match the approved design, with current monitoring and prior failure-test evidence. HYB-03: Availability objectives account for provider, facility and routing dependencies. HYB-04: Each trust connection has an owner, purpose and reviewed reachability analysis. HYB-05: Administrative access meets approved identity and network requirements, including emergency paths. CMP-01: Runtime identity and metadata follow the approved baseline; exported values are handled as sensitive. CMP-02: All privileged host access paths are covered by current identity, MFA and lifecycle requirements. CMP-03: Image provenance and boot controls meet the adopted platform baseline. CMP-04: The approved remediation timelines are met across the entire VM population, including unmanaged hosts. CMP-05: Data-bearing compute resources have approved protection, encryption and recovery arrangements. GKE-01: Control-plane access matches the documented threat model and approved administrator population. GKE-02: RBAC and admission enforcement constrain the intended workloads and administrators. GKE-03: Workloads have appropriately scoped identities and cannot rely on unnecessarily privileged node credentials. GKE-04: The cluster and node population follows an approved support and upgrade policy with controlled exclusions. GKE-05: Isolation and recovery requirements are evidenced at workload level, including persistent state. RUN-01: Public invocation and runtime privileges match the application's approved exposure. RUN-02: Each function and trigger has controlled invocation and maintained runtime dependencies. RUN-03: Automated jobs have least-privileged identities, reviewed destinations and failure handling. RUN-04: Authorized publishers and subscribers, retention and delivery behavior match the approved data flow. RUN-05: Runtime dependencies, secret versions and network access follow the deployment baseline. STO-01: Public and external access is intentional and governed across IAM, ACL and signed-access paths. STO-02: The actual permission system is covered by the access review, including managed folders. STO-03: Retention and deletion recovery work together with legal requirements and operational needs; locks are assessed without changing them. STO-04: Location and encryption requirements are supported for current and historical data populations. STO-05: Material reads and transfers have the agreed authorization, telemetry and retention coverage. DAT-01: Network paths and database identities meet the approved access model for each engine. DAT-02: The selected configuration and demonstrated restore capability meet approved RPO and RTO. DAT-03: Sensitive data access is justified at dataset, table, row and column levels where required; metadata-only coverage is documented. DAT-04: Retention, processing locations and query/export use match approved data and cost policies. DAT-05: Every material data platform has an explicit evidence plan; absence of a dedicated collector is not treated as absence of risk. KEY-01: Secret access and location are justified and match the documented consuming workloads. KEY-02: Rotation and revocation operate within approved requirements and applications consume intended versions. KEY-03: Key administration and use align with the approved custody and separation model. KEY-04: Key lifecycle changes preserve required availability and approved cryptographic policy. KEY-05: The adopted encryption model is implemented where required and its operational dependencies are understood. LOG-01: The adopted logging matrix is effectively configured and inherited exemptions are explicitly reviewed. LOG-02: Required events reach approved destinations without unintended filtering or privilege gaps. LOG-03: The retention and access model satisfies the adopted evidence requirements across every copy. LOG-04: The specific event is attributable and retrievable with expected fields and timing; the sample's limits are documented. LOG-05: The audit can explain who can read or affect evidence and where visibility is incomplete. SEC-01: Finding absence is interpreted only after coverage is demonstrated; tier-dependent gaps have compensating evidence. SEC-02: Material findings receive timely owned decisions under approved response targets. SEC-03: The agreed use cases have demonstrated signal delivery and response evidence. SEC-04: Responders can identify authorized decision makers and required access during the stated scenario. SEC-05: Closure includes validation of the failed control and documented residual risk. BCP-01: Recovery objectives cover the complete service chain and have accountable owners. BCP-02: All required data has a mapped backup mechanism and approved protection from common administrative failure. BCP-03: Prior restore evidence demonstrates the agreed objective for the sampled system; missing exercises remain a gap. BCP-04: The adopted failure scenario is covered by realistic capacity and independent dependencies. BCP-05: Runbooks remain usable under the scenario and material exercise findings are resolved or accepted. DEV-01: Untrusted changes cannot silently obtain production deployment authority through the approved pipeline. DEV-02: Build privileges and secret availability are appropriate to repository trust and deployment purpose. DEV-03: Deployed artifacts have attributable provenance and reviewed vulnerabilities under the adopted policy. DEV-04: Production admission and approval requirements are effective, with controlled break-glass use. DEV-05: Material drift is identified, owned and reconciled to approved changes. AI-01: All material AI uses have owners, data classifications, model/provider records and approved purposes. AI-02: Approved data handling addresses each enabled feature and provider, with documented exceptions. AI-03: AI service privilege and exposure match the approved use and sensitive-data boundary. AI-04: Agents enforce user-specific data access and approved tool authority at execution time. AI-05: The production use has approved quality, safety and security acceptance criteria plus monitored failure handling. OPS-01: Critical user journeys have measurable objectives and actionable monitoring. OPS-02: Approved capacity scenarios are covered by current quota and realistic resource availability. OPS-03: Unsupported or soon-retiring dependencies have an approved transition or exception. OPS-04: Changes have accountable authorization and sufficient validation for their risk. OPS-05: Critical services have current operational owners and improvements tied to recurring failure modes. FIN-01: Every billed project has an accountable owner, cost center and approved billing association. FIN-02: Budget behavior and alert response match the adopted cost-control requirement; no generic assumption that every budget caps spending. FIN-03: Material costs can be assigned and reconciled with finance at the agreed level. FIN-04: Optimization recommendations account for reliability, commitment coverage and real workload demand. FIN-05: Unexpected spend has a defined detection and response path with accountable decisions. COM-01: Every adopted requirement has an applicability decision and evidence mapping approved by the accountable team. COM-02: Classification covers the material data population, with explicit unsupported or unscanned areas. COM-03: The adopted privacy requirements are supported across copies and processors; technical settings alone do not prove legal compliance. COM-04: Claims about sovereign or regulated operation match deployed controls, service eligibility and contract terms. COM-05: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains.
P05.falsification: GOV-01: Find one billing-linked or CMDB project absent from the asset export and investigate visibility before declaring it retired. GOV-02: Select one managed database and ask who proves database-user review and recoverability. GOV-03: Look for a production workload in a sandbox project or inherited development administrator access. GOV-04: Find a locally overridden constraint with no current approval. GOV-05: Select a retired project whose data export, billing liability or service account remains unexplained. IAM-01: A harmless-looking project policy conceals an organization-level group with broad access; trace a nested member. IAM-02: Choose a privileged external principal excluded from the main employee MFA policy. IAM-03: Select an offboarded contractor whose nested group still grants access. IAM-04: Challenge an emergency account dependent on the same unavailable IdP it is intended to bypass. IAM-05: Find a boundary that does not cover the permission relied on by the proposed compensating control. WID-01: A low-privileged deployer can attach or impersonate an overprivileged runtime identity. WID-02: An unused service account still has an active externally held key with no custodian. WID-03: Test the reasoning with a forked repository or different external tenant that might satisfy a weak attribute condition; do not request tokens. WID-04: Find an identity that cannot read data directly but can deploy code as an identity that can. WID-05: A key appears unused only because the relevant service's Data Access logging was disabled. ORG-01: A lower-level override or conditional tag changes the result for a sensitive project. ORG-02: An existing external grant predates a policy change and remains unexplained. ORG-03: Key creation is blocked but old externally stored keys remain active. ORG-04: A primary region is approved while backups, logs or a global endpoint fall outside the reviewed requirement. ORG-05: A custom rule exists only in dry-run or does not cover the update method being relied upon. NET-01: A deny is shadowed by a higher-priority allow, or an apparent allow targets no instances. NET-02: A protective policy exists but is unattached or all material rules run in preview. NET-03: A private VM reaches an unintended destination through NAT or a transit route. NET-04: A protected project has an unrestricted service path, bridge or broad ingress identity condition. NET-05: A critical subnet or deny rule has no logging while a dashboard suggests complete network visibility. HYB-01: A service-project deployer can alter shared host-network security unexpectedly. HYB-02: Two apparently redundant tunnels depend on the same unprotected peer device or connection. HYB-03: Nominally redundant attachments share a failure domain omitted from the design. HYB-04: A new peering or exported default route extends access beyond the approved boundary. HYB-05: An external address and permissive rule bypass the documented administrative gateway. CMP-01: A VM uses a default overprivileged identity or a project SSH key unexpectedly applies. CMP-02: A compliant OS Login setting coexists with an unmanaged local administrator account. CMP-03: A production image is outside the approved pipeline or an integrity exception has no owner. CMP-04: A healthy patch dashboard excludes an instance with no inventory agent. CMP-05: An unattached sensitive disk or critical instance lacks the expected backup association. GKE-01: A private-node cluster still has an unintended public control-plane access path. GKE-02: A namespace owner can create a privileged workload or bind an unintended cluster role. GKE-03: A workload without its own grant can obtain access through an excessive node identity or deployment permission. GKE-04: An apparently current control plane masks old nodes or a long-lived maintenance exclusion. GKE-05: A network-policy capability is enabled but a sensitive namespace has no effective policy, or its volumes are outside backup scope. RUN-01: A load balancer is protected while the underlying service remains invokable directly. RUN-02: An event path or old function generation is omitted from the application inventory. RUN-03: A scheduler can call an unintended authenticated endpoint or silently fails without owner response. RUN-04: An external push endpoint or dead-letter topic retains sensitive data outside the documented boundary. RUN-05: A new revision uses an unreviewed secret version or broad egress and remains outside the operating review. STO-01: Public prevention is enabled but long-lived signed URLs or legacy object ACL exposure are absent from the review. STO-02: A project-level review overlooks a bucket or managed-folder grant, or assumes IAM describes every object ACL. STO-03: A lifecycle action removes recoverable versions before the required recovery window. STO-04: An object predates the default key change or a key's location conflicts with the assumed recovery design. STO-05: An apparently inactive public object path produces no authenticated access log and is misclassified as unused. DAT-01: A private instance has an unmanaged database administrator or a TLS mode weaker than the documented baseline. DAT-02: A successful backup exists but point-in-time recovery is unavailable for the incident window. DAT-03: An authorized view or broad dataset grant bypasses the intended interpretation of a masking control. DAT-04: A dataset expiry looks compliant while extracted tables persist in another project or bucket. DAT-05: A critical Firestore or Bigtable service is omitted because only SQL instances were enumerated. KEY-01: A broad project-level Secret Accessor grant exposes unrelated application secrets. KEY-02: A configured rotation topic has no functioning subscriber or workloads still use an old enabled version. KEY-03: A data administrator can also grant themselves decryption access to the same sensitive dataset. KEY-04: A retained backup depends on a key version scheduled for destruction before retention ends. KEY-05: A CMEK label is present while the service resource uses provider-managed encryption, or EKM recovery is untested. LOG-01: An empty project auditConfig is interpreted without inspecting inherited settings, or an exemption suppresses the chosen principal. LOG-02: A central sink exists but its writer lacks destination access or its filter excludes the target event. LOG-03: Only global buckets were checked while a regional bucket holds the relevant events for a shorter period. LOG-04: The source event is present but disappears after routing, or the sampled log window omits the ticket time. LOG-05: The collector receives no private entries because it lacks Private Logs Viewer permissions. SEC-01: An empty finding list comes from a location without the organization's findings or a disabled detector. SEC-02: A long-lived mute hides a recurring public exposure with no expiry or risk acceptance. SEC-03: A detection rule is enabled but depends on a disabled Data Access log source. SEC-04: A responder's emergency credentials depend on the affected identity service or cannot access the evidence project. SEC-05: A closed incident recurs with the same underlying access path. BCP-01: A database meets its RTO while identity or DNS recovery prevents the business application from operating. BCP-02: The same compromised administrator can erase production data and every retained backup. BCP-03: A report says successful but omits application integrity checks or restores only an empty database. BCP-04: A secondary region shares a key, network or quota bottleneck that prevents recovery. BCP-05: An offline recovery step requires a console or repository available only in the failed environment. DEV-01: A pull request can edit the pipeline that runs with a production service account. DEV-02: An untrusted build can impersonate the same identity that deploys production. DEV-03: A clean repository summary excludes the exact digest running in production. DEV-04: Policy exists but enforcement permits all images or a production target bypasses the pipeline. DEV-05: A console change weakens a guardrail while the repository still shows the compliant setting. AI-01: An application calls a managed model API without a dedicated endpoint and is missed by endpoint inventory. AI-02: A zero-retention assertion overlooks grounding, abuse-monitoring or optional logging behavior. AI-03: An endpoint deployer can substitute a model that runs under a more privileged identity. AI-04: A prompt or retrieved document can cause a tool to access another user's data or perform an unapproved action. AI-05: A model passes generic quality tests but fails the business's sensitive-data or tool-authorization scenarios. OPS-01: An infrastructure dashboard is green while the business transaction is unavailable. OPS-02: A failover region has nominal architecture support but insufficient quota or capacity reservations. OPS-03: A function runtime or GKE node pool remains unsupported despite a maintained application repository. OPS-04: A sensitive console change bypassed normal deployment approval without emergency review. OPS-05: A labeled owner has left or a repeated failure has no tracked corrective action. FIN-01: A project absent from the operations register still produces charges. FIN-02: An alerts-only threshold is mistaken for an enforced stop, or notification reaches an unattended mailbox. FIN-03: Unlabeled shared infrastructure or credits distort the reported cost allocation. FIN-04: An idle-looking disaster recovery resource is proposed for removal without its recovery role. FIN-05: A compromised workload can consume large resources before anyone acts on the cost alert. COM-01: A provider attestation is offered as proof that customer IAM or retention configuration complies. COM-02: A current discovery dashboard excludes a new project, unstructured store or encrypted dataset. COM-03: A deleted primary record persists in extracts, logs or a downstream AI dataset without an approved retention basis. COM-04: A project label claims a regulated package while the workload or service is outside its supported boundary. COM-05: A high-severity finding relies on truncated data or is marked closed after a change ticket without retest evidence.

P06.title: Review operating effectiveness
P06.procedure: LOG-04: Select a known historical approved administrative or data event from a ticket. Trace it through source logging, sink routing, destination and detection within a bounded UTC window. SEC-03: Map priority threats to required logs, analytics, alert routes and past incident or exercise records. Inspect existing test results rather than injecting attacks. BCP-03: Read existing backup metadata and hash supplied prior restore reports. Review restored scope, timestamp, data integrity checks, elapsed time and business acceptance.
P06.criterion: LOG-04: The specific event is attributable and retrievable with expected fields and timing; the sample's limits are documented. SEC-03: The agreed use cases have demonstrated signal delivery and response evidence. BCP-03: Prior restore evidence demonstrates the agreed objective for the sampled system; missing exercises remain a gap.
P06.falsification: LOG-04: The source event is present but disappears after routing, or the sampled log window omits the ticket time. SEC-03: A detection rule is enabled but depends on a disabled Data Access log source. BCP-03: A report says successful but omits application integrity checks or restores only an empty database.

P07.title: Challenge findings
P07.procedure: IAM-01: Read organization, all ancestor folders, project and resource policies. Expand groups through authorized directory evidence and inspect custom role permissions, conditions, deny and principal boundary policies. STO-01: Join bucket metadata, IAM bindings, inherited public access prevention and approved external-sharing uses. If uniform access is off, request object ACL metadata separately; do not download objects. COM-05: Check findings against criteria, affected population, reproducible evidence and contrary explanations. Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure.
P07.criterion: IAM-01: Each effective privileged access path is justified, assigned to an accountable identity and periodically reviewed. STO-01: Public and external access is intentional and governed across IAM, ACL and signed-access paths. COM-05: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains.
P07.falsification: IAM-01: A harmless-looking project policy conceals an organization-level group with broad access; trace a nested member. STO-01: Public prevention is enabled but long-lived signed URLs or legacy object ACL exposure are absent from the review. COM-05: A high-severity finding relies on truncated data or is marked closed after a change ticket without retest evidence.

P08.title: Prioritize and agree actions
P08.procedure: SEC-02: Sample active findings, muted records and ticket links. Evaluate severity, exploitability, asset criticality, owner, age and suppression justification. COM-05: Check findings against criteria, affected population, reproducible evidence and contrary explanations. Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure.
P08.criterion: SEC-02: Material findings receive timely owned decisions under approved response targets. COM-05: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains.
P08.falsification: SEC-02: A long-lived mute hides a recurring public exposure with no expiry or risk acceptance. COM-05: A high-severity finding relies on truncated data or is marked closed after a change ticket without retest evidence.

P09.title: Report and hand over
P09.procedure: COM-05: Check findings against criteria, affected population, reproducible evidence and contrary explanations. Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure. GOV-02: Map each material service to customer, Google and supplier duties, including data protection, IAM, patching and recovery. Assign evidence owners rather than treating managed services as fully outsourced security.
P09.criterion: COM-05: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains. GOV-02: The responsibility matrix covers all material services and has accountable owners.
P09.falsification: COM-05: A high-severity finding relies on truncated data or is marked closed after a change ticket without retest evidence. GOV-02: Select one managed database and ask who proves database-user review and recoverability.

Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure.
P10.criterion: BCP-03: Prior restore evidence demonstrates the agreed objective for the sampled system; missing exercises remain a gap. COM-05: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains.

R01-S01.title: Establish organizational ownership and scope
R01-S01.procedure: GOV-01: Reconcile organization, folders, project numbers, business owners, lifecycle state and billing inventory with the signed scope. Record separately projects visible to the collector and the expected population.
R01-S01.criterion: GOV-01: Every expected project has a disposition, owner and applicable control set; unexplained inventory gaps remain open.
R01-S01.falsification: GOV-01: Find one billing-linked or CMDB project absent from the asset export and investigate visibility before declaring it retired.

R01-S02.title: Review project lifecycle and shutdown
R01-S02.procedure: GOV-05: Inspect labels, lifecycle states, enabled services and billing links. Trace creation approval, handover and one past retirement to retained evidence and revoked access.
R01-S02.criterion: GOV-05: Creation and retirement records reconcile to inventory without orphaned ownership, data or access.
R01-S02.falsification: GOV-05: Select a retired project whose data export, billing liability or service account remains unexplained.

R01-S03.title: Reconcile billing and project accountability
R01-S03.procedure: FIN-01: Read billing associations for approved projects and compare with finance-approved account and cost-center records. Billing account scope requires explicit independent approval.
R01-S03.criterion: FIN-01: Every billed project has an accountable owner, cost center and approved billing association.
R01-S03.falsification: FIN-01: A project absent from the operations register still produces charges.

R01-S04.title: Review resource locations and sovereignty
R01-S04.procedure: ORG-04: Map actual resource locations, backups and service-supported location constraints to contractual requirements. Identify global services and processing paths that need separate analysis.
R01-S04.criterion: ORG-04: Approved location requirements apply to the relevant resource types and operational copies; unsupported services are documented.
R01-S04.falsification: ORG-04: A primary region is approved while backups, logs or a global endpoint fall outside the reviewed requirement.

R01-S05.title: Review audit evidence and assurance closure
R01-S05.procedure: COM-05: Check findings against criteria, affected population, reproducible evidence and contrary explanations. Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure.
R01-S05.criterion: COM-05: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains.
R01-S05.falsification: COM-05: A high-severity finding relies on truncated data or is marked closed after a change ticket without retest evidence.

R02-S01.title: Resolve inherited privileged access
R02-S01.procedure: IAM-01: Read organization, all ancestor folders, project and resource policies. Expand groups through authorized directory evidence and inspect custom role permissions, conditions, deny and principal boundary policies.
R02-S01.criterion: IAM-01: Each effective privileged access path is justified, assigned to an accountable identity and periodically reviewed.
R02-S01.falsification: IAM-01: A harmless-looking project policy conceals an organization-level group with broad access; trace a nested member.

R02-S02.title: Assess deny and principal access boundaries
R02-S02.procedure: IAM-05: Reconcile allow bindings with explicit deny rules, exceptions, principal-set bindings and boundary enforcement versions using resource metadata and owner exports when not inventoried.
R02-S02.criterion: IAM-05: Access analysis includes applicable allow, deny and boundary effects; unsupported permission coverage is acknowledged.
R02-S02.falsification: IAM-05: Find a boundary that does not cover the permission relied on by the proposed compensating control.

R02-S03.title: Inventory service account ownership
R02-S03.procedure: WID-01: Map service accounts, default identities, attached workloads and impersonation grants to owners and intended permissions. Inspect both use and administration of each identity.
R02-S03.criterion: WID-01: Privileged machine identities have specific purposes and accountable owners; default identities receive no unexplained broad access.
R02-S03.falsification: WID-01: A low-privileged deployer can attach or impersonate an overprivileged runtime identity.

R02-S04.title: Validate federation trust boundaries
R02-S04.procedure: WID-03: Inspect workload pools and provider issuer, audience, attribute mapping and condition. Trace external subject claims to IAM grants and repository or cloud ownership.
R02-S04.criterion: WID-03: Trust restricts intended external tenants and subjects; broad pools and impersonation grants are justified.
R02-S04.falsification: WID-03: Test the reasoning with a forked repository or different external tenant that might satisfy a weak attribute condition; do not request tokens.

R02-S05.title: Inspect service account escalation paths
R02-S05.procedure: WID-04: Review serviceAccountUser, token creation, workload deployment and project-level permissions together. Trace who can modify code running as a sensitive service identity.
R02-S05.criterion: WID-04: Privilege reviews cover combined deployment and identity capabilities, including cross-project service accounts.
R02-S05.falsification: WID-04: Find an identity that cannot read data directly but can deploy code as an identity that can.

R03-S01.title: Resolve effective firewall exposure
R03-S01.procedure: NET-01: Review VPC rules, hierarchical policies, target tags or service accounts, priorities, direction and disabled status. Join to routes, instance interfaces and approved service exposure.
R03-S01.criterion: NET-01: Public and lateral paths are justified after effective rule evaluation; a single broad rule is a review candidate, not automatic proof of reachability.
R03-S01.falsification: NET-01: A deny is shadowed by a higher-priority allow, or an apparent allow targets no instances.

R03-S02.title: Assess external application protection
R03-S02.procedure: NET-02: Map external forwarding rules to backend services and Cloud Armor policy attachment. Review rule action, preview mode, bypass endpoints, TLS configuration and owner-approved exposure.
R03-S02.criterion: NET-02: Each critical public service has the agreed protections on its actual serving path.
R03-S02.falsification: NET-02: A protective policy exists but is unattached or all material rules run in preview.

R03-S03.title: Review Cloud Run exposure and identity
R03-S03.procedure: RUN-01: Inspect service ingress, revision configuration, authentication/IAM and runtime identities across all approved regions. Review direct service URLs and load-balancer paths together.
R03-S03.criterion: RUN-01: Public invocation and runtime privileges match the application's approved exposure.
R03-S03.falsification: RUN-01: A load balancer is protected while the underlying service remains invokable directly.

R03-S04.title: Assess public and external bucket access
R03-S04.procedure: STO-01: Join bucket metadata, IAM bindings, inherited public access prevention and approved external-sharing uses. If uniform access is off, request object ACL metadata separately; do not download objects.
R03-S04.criterion: STO-01: Public and external access is intentional and governed across IAM, ACL and signed-access paths.
R03-S04.falsification: STO-01: Public prevention is enabled but long-lived signed URLs or legacy object ACL exposure are absent from the review.

R03-S05.title: Review BigQuery access and fine-grained controls
R03-S05.procedure: DAT-03: Use dataset and table asset metadata plus approved exports of row policies, policy tags, masking rules and authorized views. Trace inherited IAM, dataset ACLs and data-sharing links.
R03-S05.criterion: DAT-03: Sensitive data access is justified at dataset, table, row and column levels where required; metadata-only coverage is documented.
R03-S05.falsification: DAT-03: An authorized view or broad dataset grant bypasses the intended interpretation of a masking control.

R04-S01.title: Verify Data Access audit coverage
R04-S01.procedure: LOG-01: Read organization, ancestor-folder and project auditConfigs, service exceptions and exempted principals. Map enabled services to the required ADMIN_READ, DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE coverage.
R04-S01.criterion: LOG-01: The adopted logging matrix is effectively configured and inherited exemptions are explicitly reviewed.
R04-S01.falsification: LOG-01: An empty project auditConfig is interpreted without inspecting inherited settings, or an exemption suppresses the chosen principal.

R04-S02.title: Review routing sinks and exclusions
R04-S02.procedure: LOG-02: Inspect project and organization sinks, inclusion and exclusion filters, destination ownership and writer grants. Review intercepting behavior and aggregated child scope.
R04-S02.criterion: LOG-02: Required events reach approved destinations without unintended filtering or privilege gaps.
R04-S02.falsification: LOG-02: A central sink exists but its writer lacks destination access or its filter excludes the target event.

R04-S03.title: Assess retention location and protected access
R04-S03.procedure: LOG-03: Inspect log bucket retention, location, access restrictions and lock state across all used locations. Reconcile SIEM and archive retention outside Cloud Logging.
R04-S03.criterion: LOG-03: The retention and access model satisfies the adopted evidence requirements across every copy.
R04-S03.falsification: LOG-03: Only global buckets were checked while a regional bucket holds the relevant events for a shorter period.

R04-S04.title: Prove an existing event's end-to-end trace
R04-S04.procedure: LOG-04: Select a known historical approved administrative or data event from a ticket. Trace it through source logging, sink routing, destination and detection within a bounded UTC window.
R04-S04.criterion: LOG-04: The specific event is attributable and retrievable with expected fields and timing; the sample's limits are documented.
R04-S04.falsification: LOG-04: The source event is present but disappears after routing, or the sampled log window omits the ticket time.

R04-S05.title: Assess integrity and evidence visibility
R04-S05.procedure: LOG-05: Review log administration, private-log viewing, deletion and sink modification privileges. Reconcile coverage counts and missing-access errors before concluding about activity.
R04-S05.criterion: LOG-05: The audit can explain who can read or affect evidence and where visibility is incomplete.
R04-S05.falsification: LOG-05: The collector receives no private entries because it lacks Private Logs Viewer permissions.

R05-S01.title: Assess classification and data discovery
R05-S01.procedure: COM-02: Compare data classification and existing discovery/profile results with storage, databases, datasets and AI inventories. Inspect coverage, location, job recency and exclusions without initiating scans.
R05-S01.criterion: COM-02: Classification covers the material data population, with explicit unsupported or unscanned areas.
R05-S01.falsification: COM-02: A current discovery dashboard excludes a new project, unstructured store or encrypted dataset.

R05-S02.title: Inspect bucket encryption and location
R05-S02.procedure: STO-04: Map storage location, default key references and object-encryption evidence to requirements. A default CMEK setting alone does not prove all existing objects use that key.
R05-S02.criterion: STO-04: Location and encryption requirements are supported for current and historical data populations.
R05-S02.falsification: STO-04: An object predates the default key change or a key's location conflicts with the assumed recovery design.

R05-S03.title: Review BigQuery access and fine-grained controls
R05-S03.procedure: DAT-03: Use dataset and table asset metadata plus approved exports of row policies, policy tags, masking rules and authorized views. Trace inherited IAM, dataset ACLs and data-sharing links.
R05-S03.criterion: DAT-03: Sensitive data access is justified at dataset, table, row and column levels where required; metadata-only coverage is documented.
R05-S03.falsification: DAT-03: An authorized view or broad dataset grant bypasses the intended interpretation of a masking control.

R05-S04.title: Assess KMS purpose and separation of duties
R05-S04.procedure: KEY-03: Inspect key rings, algorithms, protection level, IAM and encrypt/decrypt versus administration permissions. Map key projects and service agents to protected resources.
R05-S04.criterion: KEY-03: Key administration and use align with the approved custody and separation model.
R05-S04.falsification: KEY-03: A data administrator can also grant themselves decryption access to the same sensitive dataset.

R05-S05.title: Review key lifecycle and availability
R05-S05.procedure: KEY-04: Review primary versions, rotation and destruction schedule evidence. Reconcile disabled or pending-destruction versions with active data and backup dependencies.
R05-S05.criterion: KEY-04: Key lifecycle changes preserve required availability and approved cryptographic policy.
R05-S05.falsification: KEY-04: A retained backup depends on a key version scheduled for destruction before retention ends.

R06-S01.title: Map recovery objectives to dependencies
R06-S01.procedure: BCP-01: Join critical services to data stores, identities, keys, DNS, networking and provider dependencies. Obtain business-approved RPO and RTO, including data-loss tolerance.
R06-S01.criterion: BCP-01: Recovery objectives cover the complete service chain and have accountable owners.
R06-S01.falsification: BCP-01: A database meets its RTO while identity or DNS recovery prevents the business application from operating.

R06-S02.title: Review backup coverage and immutability
R06-S02.procedure: BCP-02: Reconcile data-bearing resources with snapshot, SQL backup, GKE backup and Backup and DR metadata. Inspect retention, separation, vault protection and administration.
R06-S02.criterion: BCP-02: All required data has a mapped backup mechanism and approved protection from common administrative failure.
R06-S02.falsification: BCP-02: The same compromised administrator can erase production data and every retained backup.

R06-S03.title: Assess restore evidence
R06-S03.procedure: BCP-03: Read existing backup metadata and hash supplied prior restore reports. Review restored scope, timestamp, data integrity checks, elapsed time and business acceptance.
R06-S03.criterion: BCP-03: Prior restore evidence demonstrates the agreed objective for the sampled system; missing exercises remain a gap.
R06-S03.falsification: BCP-03: A report says successful but omits application integrity checks or restores only an empty database.

R06-S04.title: Review regional and zonal failure readiness
R06-S04.procedure: BCP-04: Inspect multi-zone or regional configurations and compare capacity, quotas and dependencies to the failover design. Evaluate existing exercises and their assumptions.
R06-S04.criterion: BCP-04: The adopted failure scenario is covered by realistic capacity and independent dependencies.
R06-S04.falsification: BCP-04: A secondary region shares a key, network or quota bottleneck that prevents recovery.

R06-S05.title: Assess recovery operations and ownership
R06-S05.procedure: BCP-05: Review recovery runbooks, access prerequisites, communications and retrospective improvements. Verify named owners can locate retained evidence and necessary approvals.
R06-S05.criterion: BCP-05: Runbooks remain usable under the scenario and material exercise findings are resolved or accepted.
R06-S05.falsification: BCP-05: An offline recovery step requires a console or repository available only in the failed environment.

R07-S01.title: Review source and build trigger trust
R07-S01.procedure: DEV-01: Inspect Cloud Build triggers, event filters, approval settings, repository connections and execution identities. Reconcile branch protection and contributor permissions from the source platform.
R07-S01.criterion: DEV-01: Untrusted changes cannot silently obtain production deployment authority through the approved pipeline.
R07-S01.falsification: DEV-01: A pull request can edit the pipeline that runs with a production service account.

R07-S02.title: Assess build identity and secrets
R07-S02.procedure: DEV-02: Review build service accounts, worker pools, network access and secret references. Inspect a bounded sample of historical builds without triggering builds.
R07-S02.criterion: DEV-02: Build privileges and secret availability are appropriate to repository trust and deployment purpose.
R07-S02.falsification: DEV-02: An untrusted build can impersonate the same identity that deploys production.

R07-S03.title: Assess deployment approvals and admission
R07-S03.procedure: DEV-04: Inspect delivery pipelines, Binary Authorization policy and approved attestor evidence. Trace one deployed artifact to source, build, approval and admission result.
R07-S03.criterion: DEV-04: Production admission and approval requirements are effective, with controlled break-glass use.
R07-S03.falsification: DEV-04: Policy exists but enforcement permits all images or a production target bypasses the pipeline.

R07-S04.title: Assess agent tools and retrieval boundaries
R07-S04.procedure: AI-04: Use application-supplied agent manifests, tool definitions, retrieval ACL design and existing evaluation traces. Review delegated identity and approval of consequential actions without invoking tools.
R07-S04.criterion: AI-04: Agents enforce user-specific data access and approved tool authority at execution time.
R07-S04.falsification: AI-04: A prompt or retrieved document can cause a tool to access another user's data or perform an unapproved action.

R07-S05.title: Review AI evaluation and operational oversight
R07-S05.procedure: AI-05: Inspect model/version approvals, evaluation criteria, safety filters, monitoring, rollback and incident records. Sample completed evaluations for representative failure modes.
R07-S05.criterion: AI-05: The production use has approved quality, safety and security acceptance criteria plus monitored failure handling.
R07-S05.falsification: AI-05: A model passes generic quality tests but fails the business's sensitive-data or tool-authorization scenarios.

R08-S01.title: Assess Security Command Center coverage
R08-S01.procedure: SEC-01: Reconcile activation scope, edition, data location, services, detectors and project population with expected coverage. Read findings and record activation or permission failures.
R08-S01.criterion: SEC-01: Finding absence is interpreted only after coverage is demonstrated; tier-dependent gaps have compensating evidence.
R08-S01.falsification: SEC-01: An empty finding list comes from a location without the organization's findings or a disabled detector.

R08-S02.title: Validate detection use cases
R08-S02.procedure: SEC-03: Map priority threats to required logs, analytics, alert routes and past incident or exercise records. Inspect existing test results rather than injecting attacks.
R08-S02.criterion: SEC-03: The agreed use cases have demonstrated signal delivery and response evidence.
R08-S02.falsification: SEC-03: A detection rule is enabled but depends on a disabled Data Access log source.

R08-S03.title: Assess observability against service objectives
R08-S03.procedure: OPS-01: Join workload inventory to approved SLIs, SLOs, dashboards, alerts and escalation owners from monitoring exports. Review existing incidents and error budgets.
R08-S03.criterion: OPS-01: Critical user journeys have measurable objectives and actionable monitoring.
R08-S03.falsification: OPS-01: An infrastructure dashboard is green while the business transaction is unavailable.

R08-S04.title: Review budgets and spend control behavior
R08-S04.procedure: FIN-02: Inspect budgets for explicitly approved accounts, filters, thresholds and recipients. Determine whether a budget is alerts-only or a supported spend-cap configuration and inspect actual handling.
R08-S04.criterion: FIN-02: Budget behavior and alert response match the adopted cost-control requirement; no generic assumption that every budget caps spending.
R08-S04.falsification: FIN-02: An alerts-only threshold is mistaken for an enforced stop, or notification reaches an unattended mailbox.

R08-S05.title: Review audit evidence and assurance closure
R08-S05.procedure: COM-05: Check findings against criteria, affected population, reproducible evidence and contrary explanations. Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure.
R08-S05.criterion: COM-05: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains.
R08-S05.falsification: COM-05: A high-severity finding relies on truncated data or is marked closed after a change ticket without retest evidence.
